nodes.label: Meet transcripts via Workspace Events
nodes.rationale: Transcription is an admin-enabled Workspace feature; if unavailable the Source seam lets sources/meet.py be a no-op, exactly as v5's meet_ingest.pull_and_stage degrades.

nodes.label: The four minimal OAuth scopes
nodes.rationale: Request the minimum; every additional scope makes an admin allowlist request harder to approve, and all four are read-only which helps when asking for approval.

nodes.label: Coding conventions
nodes.rationale: Tests must run with no live GCP, database, or LLM; a test requiring live credentials is a broken test. v5 achieved this for 363 tests and the property must not regress.

nodes.label: Never pass event= to structlog
nodes.rationale: event= collides with structlog's reserved message field and raises TypeError at call time - this was a real production 500 in v5.

nodes.label: Loopback redirect and prompt=consent
nodes.rationale: The out-of-band flow is deprecated, and without an explicit prompt=consent Google may not return a refresh token on a repeat authorisation.

nodes.label: Secret handling rules
nodes.rationale: Never log a token, not even truncated; the refresh-token secret keeps a short version retention policy because old versions are expired credentials.

nodes.label: Bug 3: structlog reserved kwarg
nodes.rationale: log.info(..., event=event) raises TypeError at call time - a real HTTP 500 on /webhook/github that every test missed by calling the handler directly.

nodes.label: Hand-rolled OAuth over httpx
nodes.rationale: Three reasons over google_auth_oauthlib.InstalledAppFlow: CLAUDE.md mandates httpx.AsyncClient and the Google client libraries are synchronous httplib2; the exchange/refresh helpers are reused verbatim by Phase 5's refresh_tokens job; and the script must import nothing from meeting_notes/ because that package is empty until Phase 2.

nodes.label: Meet: reachable vs transcripts-present
nodes.rationale: An HTTP 200 with zero conference records means the API is reachable but the tenant has no transcripts - a different answer from 'the call failed' - and conflating them would misreport a Phase 0.5 exit criterion.

nodes.label: No-secrets-in-output guarantee (spike)
nodes.rationale: Proven by test, not by inspection: the report must not contain the token, not even a truncated prefix. The token file is also opened 0600 rather than chmod'd afterwards, because write-then-chmod leaves a window in which it is world-readable.

nodes.label: Leak-canary secret test
nodes.rationale: An earlier draft asserted the substring SECRET never appears, which false-positives immediately because the variable is named GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET and printing the name is the point; the invariant is that the value never appears, so values carry a canary that cannot collide with any variable name.

nodes.label: graphify maintenance discipline
nodes.rationale: Commit GRAPH_REPORT.md and graph.json but never graphify-out/cache/; v5 tracked ~180 cache files by accident.

nodes.label: doctor exit code contract
nodes.rationale: 0 all pass, 1 at least one FAIL, 2 warnings only; CI and make demo both refuse to proceed on 1.

nodes.label: doctor.py check contract
nodes.rationale: The single highest-leverage file for the clone experience: it answers 'why can't I run this?' before the user has to read a stack trace. Every FAIL carries a runnable command or a document anchor, and credentials are reported set/unset/expired with no value ever printed.

nodes.label: Standing exit criterion (spec)
nodes.rationale: What prevents the retrofit; the local stack is exercised continuously rather than rotting.

nodes.label: The three-tier contract
nodes.rationale: Higher tiers are additive, never prerequisites; tier 0 is the promise and must work offline on a clean clone with no .env edits.

nodes.label: Injected-probe check design
nodes.rationale: Every check is a pure function returning a CheckResult with its environment probe injected as a parameter, so the whole suite runs with no Docker, no network, and no gcloud.

nodes.label: Airbyte residue to delete
nodes.rationale: v5's db.py carries scar tissue from Airbyte writing hash-suffixed table names; processed_gmail_ids stays because it survives a full re-sync independently of Airbyte.

nodes.label: Deferred to v2: dev_agent and action_agent
nodes.norm_label: deferred to v2: dev_agent and action_agent
nodes.rationale: The pipeline has to be solid first, but the provenance schema ships in v1 anyway because provenance cannot be backfilled - a merge before the schema exists is lost forever.

nodes.label: Bug 9: Leiden over-fragmentation
nodes.rationale: Community detection collapsed to all-singletons; check v5's git history for the fix.

nodes.label: Order of porting
nodes.rationale: Pure modules first for an early green suite, then I/O, LLM seam, connectors, pipeline, intelligence, API. Do not start with the connectors - they depend on Phase 0.5's outcome.

nodes.label: Personal-then-Onix deployment context
nodes.rationale: Infrastructure project and data-source Workspace account are deliberately different, which makes portability a first-class design constraint rather than a later concern.

nodes.label: Property graph schema
nodes.rationale: Sourced from the live v5 graph rather than v5's own docs, because the live graph proved more accurate. Edge vocabulary is deliberately aligned with Matteo's engagement ontology so the graph is legible to anyone who knows it.

nodes.label: meeting-notes-gcp v6
nodes.rationale: v6 is a deliberate fresh-repo port of v5, not a rewrite: the deployment target moved from a MacBook to GCP, so Airbyte and in-process scheduling could not survive, while Memgraph+MAGE, FastAPI, the extraction prompts and the test suite are assets worth carrying across.

nodes.label: Repository layout
nodes.rationale: jobs/ and api/ are entrypoints only; a job file past ~50 lines means the logic belongs in the meeting_notes package.

nodes.label: v1-v6 version lineage
nodes.rationale: v3 and v4/v5 repos are read-only reference so that no local-first or Airbyte assumption leaks back in by accident.

nodes.label: Migration to the Onix project
nodes.rationale: An Internal client removes expiry, the test-user list and verification all at once; everything else is unchanged, which is the whole point of portability as a design constraint.

nodes.label: StagedRecord normalisation question
nodes.rationale: v5's four Raw* models overlap; since v6 owns every connector they normalise to one row shape with a per-source adapter. Decide it before writing db.py - it affects every connector.

nodes.label: db.py dual-mode connection
nodes.rationale: Decided now rather than during Phase 3 because a data-layer shape settled after the connectors exist is far more expensive to change.

nodes.label: Intent-to-skill map
nodes.rationale: Non-Claude-Code agents get an explicit intent table because they do not read the plugin skill listing.

nodes.label: Live v5 graph inventory
nodes.rationale: Inspected 2026-08-13, more accurate than v5's own docs. 61 of 84 meetings are standups and AgentRun is inflated by bug 2, so any PageRank or community result from it is distorted.

nodes.label: v5 to v6 port map
nodes.rationale: Lift / Adapt / Rewrite / Drop per module, so every carried-over file is consciously chosen.

nodes.label: Module boundaries
nodes.rationale: These boundaries held perfectly in v5, so they are carried unchanged: SQL only in db.py, generic Cypher only in graph_client.py, MAGE CALL only in graph_algorithms.py, Jira REST only in jira_client.py, os.environ only in config.py, LLM clients only in llm_client.py.

nodes.label: Person.tracked governance gate
nodes.rationale: Aggregates are the default and naming individuals is opt-in, so every per-person analytic must filter on tracked = true.

nodes.label: Lowercased Topic MERGE key
nodes.rationale: Raw case fragmented single topics across multiple nodes in v5 and silently understated every insight query.

nodes.label: Deterministic uuid5_id node ids
nodes.rationale: Deterministic ids make reprocessing idempotent under MERGE; writer/reader id drift is a known past bug class that cost real debugging time twice.

nodes.label: OAuth user type follows the project/account split
nodes.norm_label: oauth user type follows the project/account split
nodes.rationale: A GCP project and a Google account are independent, but where the project lives determines whether the client can be Internal (no verification, no expiry) or only External.

nodes.label: The 7-day refresh token problem
nodes.rationale: External + Testing issues refresh tokens that expire after exactly 7 days; Gmail's restricted scopes make publishing to Production require verification plus a third-party security assessment. Expiry must be loud - a pipeline that silently stops for four days is worse than one that pages you weekly.

nodes.label: Workspace admin third-party app block
nodes.rationale: If 'unconfigured third-party apps' is set to block, an OAuth client from an unknown personal project cannot access Onix data at all no matter how correct the code is - a hard stop, and the reason Phase 0.5 exists. Workspace trust and Google verification are two separate gates.

nodes.label: Bug 1: ASSIGNED_TO never forms
nodes.rationale: The Cypher matches Person by email but the extractor emits display names, so the live edge count is zero. Fix: resolve action.owner through person_resolver before the write.

nodes.label: Bug 2: get_active_run resume loop
nodes.rationale: A successful run parks at SHIPPED, which was not in the terminal set, so every poll re-resumed it and produced 61 AgentRun nodes for one ticket.

nodes.label: Bug 8: sync_jira_issue always returned True
nodes.rationale: Returned success even when zero nodes matched, making the counters meaningless.

nodes.label: Bug 6: provenance id drift
nodes.rationale: Ids derived in one place and re-derived differently in another meant reads never found what writes created. Bit the project twice.

nodes.label: Bug 10: test-stub pollution
nodes.rationale: Test files stubbed optional dependencies behind 'if mod_name not in sys.modules', so whichever test ran first won for the whole session; conftest.py's _REAL_HTTPX fix is load-bearing.

nodes.label: Bug 7: get_ticket_provenance missing c.message
nodes.rationale: Forward and reverse traversals returned different shapes; test that their RETURN shapes match.

nodes.label: Bug 5: Topic case fragmentation
nodes.rationale: Raw-case MERGE keys made 'Migration' and 'migration' two nodes with a colliding uuid5 id.

nodes.label: Non-goals of the reproducibility design
nodes.rationale: Terraform will not create the OAuth consent screen or client, no Workspace admin approval can be automated, make demo never writes to a real Jira, and it stays single-tenant.

nodes.label: Problem: a stranger can run nothing
nodes.norm_label: problem: a stranger can run nothing
nodes.rationale: Each credential is a wall, and the first is hit before a single line of the project's actual value is visible.

nodes.label: Realistic sample meeting corpus
nodes.rationale: Not cosmetic: seeding a skewed corpus would bake v5's 73%-standup distortion into every cloner's first impression. Seeding must be idempotent.

nodes.label: Ephemeral-port loopback callback server
nodes.rationale: Binding 127.0.0.1:0 removes the 'port 8888 is busy' failure mode v5's refresh_gcal_token.py works around, since Desktop OAuth clients accept any loopback port. State is validated to prevent CSRF and the access log is silenced because it would echo the authorization code.

nodes.label: Memgraph Lab service
nodes.rationale: Lab is where a cloner inspects the demo graph, which is most of the 'wow'.

nodes.label: Local memgraph-mage service
nodes.rationale: Tag must match Phase 1's Terraform GCE VM image or MAGE procedure availability differs between local and deployed, and a nightly job that passes locally fails there.

nodes.label: Local Postgres 15 service
nodes.rationale: Postgres major version matches Cloud SQL (15) so local testing is evidence about production.

nodes.label: LLM configuration seam
nodes.rationale: One protocol (chat_json/embed) owns every backend so no module constructs its own client; temperature is pinned at 0.0 for extraction; the privacy claim is restated as 'never leaves our GCP tenancy' rather than overstated.

nodes.label: Four LLM backends behind one protocol
nodes.norm_label: four llm backends behind one protocol
nodes.rationale: Adds gemini and fake while keeping llm_client.py's protocol unchanged and its position as the only module that constructs an LLM client.

nodes.label: Local compose stack design
nodes.rationale: The API runs on the host rather than in compose so the edit-reload loop stays fast during Phases 3-8; a cloner never runs a second command to see the dashboard.

nodes.label: Reproducibility risks
nodes.rationale: Biggest: the local Memgraph image drifting from the VM image, mitigated by the same pinned tag in compose and Terraform and asserted by doctor at tier 2.

nodes.label: 768-dimensional embedding invariant
nodes.rationale: Both Memgraph vector indexes are configured for 768, so every backend must emit 768 dims or both indexes need migrating.

nodes.label: Pinned image tags taken from v5
nodes.norm_label: pinned image tags taken from v5
nodes.rationale: Tags are taken from v5's live-validated compose rather than guessed; the API deliberately does not run in compose so the edit-reload loop stays fast during Phases 3-8.

nodes.label: Bug 4: literal 'null' strings from the LLM
nodes.norm_label: bug 4: literal 'null' strings from the llm
nodes.rationale: Gemma emits the string 'null' rather than a JSON null, and a non-empty string is truthy so falsiness checks do not catch it. Verify Gemini too - do not assume immunity.

nodes.label: Unignoring docker-compose.local.yml
nodes.rationale: The *.local.* scratch rule would swallow the compose file, which is a committed first-class file, so an explicit negation is added first - before the task that creates it.

nodes.label: Hash-keyed fixture replay
nodes.rationale: Fixtures are keyed by a hash of system prompt + user content + temperature so a prompt edit produces a loud miss that raises rather than falling through to a default; record_fixtures.py regenerates in one command.
